question.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3}-x-1)^{′}=3{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-1}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(3{x}_{n}^{2}-1)-({x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-1)}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2{x}_{n}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2{x}_{0}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{0}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1)^{3}+1}{3(1)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.5.\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{2{x}_{1}^{3}+1}{3{x}_{1}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.5)^{3}+1}{3(1.5)^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{7.75}{5.75} \\  & ≈1.348,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
